key_insight: KAN variants showed no systematic discrimination advantage over a tuned MLP across datasets, although TabKAN and ReLUKAN improved AUPRC on some severely imbalanced datasets.
clinical_relevance: KANs may be useful for research on rare positive-case detection in clinical tabular data, while StandardMLP remains a strong efficiency baseline.
method: Compared nine KAN variants, a tuned StandardMLP, and Random Forest across seven medical tabular datasets.
Used 3×5 repeated stratified cross-validation with nested Bayesian hyperparameter optimization.
Evaluated AUPRC, Brier Score, and computational efficiency; assessed equivalence with a Bayesian correlated t-test and ROPE of ±0.01.
evidence_signal: Across seven datasets spanning six clinical specialties, pooled discrimination was comparable, while KAN inference took 1.20–1.48× longer per sample and used up to 12.5× more trainable parameters.
watch_item: Cross-validation benchmark results do not establish clinical benefit or deployment readiness, and KAN computational overhead may limit practical value.
paper_title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks vs. Multi-Layer Perceptrons: A Rigorous Statistical Benchmark on Clinical Tabular Data
